open_points.subject: EffectApproval status transition (`used`)
open_points.text: M24: "`approved` → `used` when the effect is sent." A11 rule 4: on restart for `in_flight`, the kernel "marks that approval `used`" while outcome is forced to `unknown`.
open_points.question: Does `used` mean "definitely sent" or "consumed/unsafe to reuse"?
options: `used` only if the kernel knows bytes were sent; recovery must keep approval `approved` when send is uncertain
`used` means the approval cannot authorize another send once an in-flight attempt existed, even if send certainty is unknown
open_points.default_guess: Treat `used` as consumed authority (second option), because recovery must avoid accidental replay.

open_points.subject: TrialCase `expected_outputs` completeness
open_points.text: M06: "`expected_outputs` ... absent when only the absence of failure is required" and A04 rule 1: "expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports".
open_points.question: When `expected_outputs` is present, must it include exactly all output ports, or can it be a subset?
options: Require exactly one expected output per declared output port
Allow subset; only listed outputs are compared
Allow empty object as distinct from absent
open_points.default_guess: Require exact full set of output ports when present.

open_points.subject: Guard value equality
open_points.text: A05 rule 1: a guarded edge enables "when that port's value equals it".
open_points.question: What exact equality semantics are required for guard comparison (type-strict JSON value equality, canonical-byte equality, or coercive comparison)?
options: Type-strict structural JSON equality with no coercion
open_points.default_guess: Type-strict structural JSON equality without coercion.

open_points.subject: HTTP header name collisions with generated headers
open_points.text: A09 rule 1 fixes sent headers (`host`, `accept-encoding`, required headers, credential header, and body headers) and forbids some duplicates, but only explicitly checks required-header duplicates and credential-vs-required at start.
open_points.question: If a required header name collides (case-insensitive) with generated headers like `host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, or `content-length`, is send refused or which value wins?
options: Refuse as manifest mismatch / pre-send failure
Allow required header to override generated header
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to send on any collision.

open_points.subject: `stored_value_bytes_max` for `many` value ports
open_points.text: A12 rule 1: "each value ... is within `stored_value_bytes_max`"; A13 rule 3: `many` is a JSON array; A15 rule 4: "A value ... above `stored_value_bytes_max`".
open_points.question: For a `many` value, is the size ceiling applied to the whole array value only, to each element, or both?
options: Both whole array and each element
open_points.default_guess: Apply ceiling to the whole serialized value only.

open_points.subject: Resume behavior when some unreachable elements cannot be resent
open_points.text: A14 rule 2: resume "sends again ... every element waiting on `service_unreachable` ... All these resends come first; only then does the run advance as A13 says."
open_points.question: During that resend pass, if one element now cannot send (e.g., grant revoked so it waits for approval, or pre-send check fails), must resume continue trying later waiting elements in the same request?
options: Continue through all waiting-unreachable elements in order, handling each independently
Stop resend pass at first non-sendable element
open_points.default_guess: Continue through all eligible elements in order.
